meta.title: Open Paint Studio — OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: Open Paint Studio: a simple open source image editor with editable vector objects, for sketches, mark-ups and floor plans. For Windows, macOS and Linux, with an API and MCP server for AI assistants.

header.label: Open source image editor
header.title: Open Paint Studio
header.tagline: Sketch, mark up and touch up, without a heavy photo editor
header.desc: A simple image editor in the spirit of MS Paint, in the OpenAEC house style. Draw, mark up and edit images, keep shapes and text editable as vector objects, and let an AI assistant join in through the API and MCP server.

slides.dark: Open Paint Studio in the dark Forge theme with a sample floor plan in which Ctrl+A has selected all objects
slides.overview: The editor with an annotated sample floor plan, the drawing tools and the colours in the Home ribbon
slides.text: Editing text directly on the canvas, with a choice of font and size, while the shapes stay editable

features.label: Features
features.heading: Light, fast and editable
features.sub: Start with the highlights or pick a topic.

draw.title: Drawing
draw.desc: Brush, eraser, fill, eyedropper, lines, rectangles and ellipses, with adjustable size, opacity and a colour palette.

text.title: Text on the canvas
text.desc: Type text straight into the image and pick font and size. The fonts are bundled, so it works offline too.

vector.title: Editable vector objects
vector.desc: Select, move, resize and restyle drawn shapes and text. Ctrl+A grabs everything at once. Export as editable SVG.

undo.title: Undo and recovery
undo.desc: Undo or redo the last 40 steps, and a draft that is kept when you close the window.

image.title: Image editing
image.desc: Crop, resize, rotate and flip. Vector objects are kept along the way.

colors.title: Colour corrections
colors.desc: Brightness, contrast, saturation, greyscale, invert and sepia.

themes.title: Five themes, two languages
themes.desc: Light, Forge, OpenAEC, Blueprint and high contrast, in Dutch and English.

ai.title: API and MCP
ai.desc: A local API with its own token and an MCP server, so an AI assistant such as Claude can open and edit images.

draw.title: Mark up in a few clicks
draw.desc: Brush, eraser, fill, eyedropper, lines, rectangles and ellipses, with adjustable size, opacity and a colour palette. Ideal for marking up a screenshot, sketching a floor plan or annotating a photo.

text.title: Text straight on the canvas
text.desc: Type text into the image and pick font and size. Click the text later to change it. The fonts are bundled, so it works without an internet connection too.

vector.title: What you draw stays editable
vector.desc: With Keep vector objects you select, move, resize and restyle shapes and text afterwards; Ctrl+A grabs everything at once. Cropping, rotating and flipping leave the objects intact, and you export them as editable SVG.

formats.title: Opens almost any image, on your own computer
formats.desc: The editor reads common images itself; for TIFF, PSD, HEIC, JPEG XL, camera RAW and more, ImageMagick is built in as WebAssembly. Nothing goes to the cloud. Export to PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG, or keep the image in IFCX.

view.title: Zoom and focus mode
view.desc: Ctrl+scroll zooms from 10% to 400%, dragging with the middle mouse button pans the canvas, and focus mode (F11) gives the drawing area the whole window.

api.title: Local API
api.desc: An API on 127.0.0.1 with a token of its own. Send the current image to the API or load a document from it; a revision check stops two programs from overwriting each other's work.

assoc.title: File associations
assoc.desc: Open an image or an IFCX/IFCXB document with a double-click in your file manager.

formats.open: PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF, HEIC/HEIF, AVIF, PSD, SVG, ICO, TGA, JPEG 2000, JPEG XL, camera RAW and IFCX/IFCXB.
formats.save: Export to PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG, or keep the image in IFCX or IFCXB.
formats.local: No upload to the cloud. Your draft is saved on your own device as you work.

download.label: Download
download.title: Download v2026.45.1
download.lead: Free and without an account. Every button starts the download right away.
download.metaWindows: Installer for Windows, 64-bit, without administrator rights
download.metaMac: Universal disk image for macOS, Apple and Intel processors
download.metaLinux: AppImage for Linux x86-64, runs on most distributions
download.mobileNote: Open Paint Studio is a desktop application for Windows, macOS and Linux. Download it on your computer; all files are listed below.

note.windows: Windows: the installer installs for the current user, without administrator rights. If WebView2 is missing, the installer installs it.
note.mac: macOS: one universal disk image for Macs with an Apple or Intel processor.
note.sha: Check a download against the SHA256SUMS file in the release.
note.services: The API and the MCP server are separate Node processes and are not part of the installers. You start them from the source code; the README explains how.

whatsnew.label: New in v2026.45.1
whatsnew.title: Its own logo and a Snap package
whatsnew.desc: Released on 6 November 2026. This version gives the app its approved logo and adds a Snap package for Linux.

logo.title: Approved app logo
logo.desc: The Snap Store logo is now used in the app, the browser version and the installers, at every size with the right colours and rounded corners.

snap.title: Snap package
snap.desc: Next to the AppImage and the .deb package, the release now carries a .snap, built from exactly the same .deb package.

version.title: One version number
version.desc: The app and all packages and installers now carry the same version number.

cost.a: Nothing. Open Paint Studio is open source under the MIT licence; the OpenAEC house style and the logo are licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0. No licence fees, no subscription and no account.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: Windows (64-bit), macOS on Apple and Intel processors, and Linux on x86-64 as an AppImage, .deb or Snap. The editor also runs as a browser app, but there is no public version of it yet; you start it yourself from the source code.

formats.q: Which files can I open and save?
formats.a: Open: PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF, HEIC/HEIF, AVIF, PSD, SVG, ICO, TGA, JPEG 2000, JPEG XL, supported camera RAW variants and IFCX/IFCXB. Export: PNG, JPEG, WebP and SVG; saving (Ctrl+S) keeps the image in IFCX. A multipage or animated file opens as a single image, and SVG and PSD become a raster image when opened.

vector.q: Do my shapes and text stay editable?
vector.a: Yes, as long as Keep vector objects is on (it is by default). Shapes, brush strokes and text stay separate objects, also after rotating, flipping or resizing. Colour corrections flatten the image; undo brings the objects back. For editable vectors outside the app, export SVG.

ai.q: Does it work with an AI assistant?
ai.a: Yes. The MCP server gives an assistant tools to create an image, draw on it, undo a step and get the result back as a PNG. The server uses the same local API as the editor. Both are separate Node processes that you start from the source code; the installers do not start them.

privacy.q: Do my images go to the cloud?
privacy.a: No. The extra image formats are read locally too, by a built-in ImageMagick in WebAssembly. Your draft is saved on your own device as you work, and the API listens on your own computer only.

size.q: How large can an image be?
size.a: A file of up to 64 MB and 64 megapixels. The working canvas is scaled down proportionally to at most 4096 pixels per side and 8 megapixels. The editor works with 8 bits per channel; HDR and layers are not kept.

lang.q: Which languages does the interface come in?
lang.a: Dutch and English, with five themes: light, Forge (dark), OpenAEC, Blueprint and high contrast.

tech.heading: Technology and licence
tech.sub: For those who want to know how it is built.

tauri.title: Tauri 2 and Rust
tauri.desc: A small desktop app that uses the system web view; the same editor also runs in the browser.

ts.title: TypeScript and Vite
ts.desc: The editor itself, with the ribbon components and themes of the OpenAEC style book.

magick.title: ImageMagick in WebAssembly
magick.desc: Reads the less common image formats locally, in a separate worker.

api.title: API and MCP
api.desc: Separate Node processes; the API listens on 127.0.0.1 only and asks for a token, the MCP server talks over stdio.

ifcx.title: IFCX
ifcx.desc: The image can be kept in an IFCX or IFCXB document, so it fits alongside building information.

tech.desc: The editor and the services are licensed under MIT; the OpenAEC house style, the logo and the components from the style book under CC BY-SA 4.0.
